findings.issue: REGRESSION on the legacy spectra path. `_rank_ticks(ax, width, B)` picks the tick caption from the spectrum WIDTH (`cap = 'B' if width == B else 'W'`), but `sv.plot_epoch_spectra` normalises the x-axis by the width only for full-spectrum records; a legacy truncated record is still normalised by `k` (sv_diagnostics.py:428 `denom = max((width if full else k) - 1, 1)`). Verified with a synthetic legacy record (B=k=64, stored width 30): ticks now read ['$1$','$W/4$','$W/2$','$3W/4$','$W$'] while x=0.25 is really rank k/4 = B/4, and the data only reach x=0.46. The old code said B/4..B, which was correct. Every legacy spectrum figure (the 4 scan notebooks + comparisons.ipynb) now carries a wrong x-axis caption, and the spec says legacy truncated records must plot as before.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the DENOMINATOR that was actually used, not the width: in `plot_sv_spectra` compute `full = spectra.shape[1] >= k` and call `_rank_ticks(ax, spectra.shape[1] if full else k, scan.B)`, or give `_rank_ticks` a `full` flag and use `cap = 'B' if denom == B else ('W' if full else 'k')`. `plot_sv_utr` (line 1186) is fine, it always normalises by the width.

findings.issue: C-A3's float32 noise floor is never drawn on the path the notebooks use, and the full spectrum is clipped at 1e-4. The noise-floor line is gated on `FLOAT32_NOISE_FLOOR >= floor` (1e-7 >= floor), and `scan_analysis.plot_sv_spectra` defaults `floor=1e-4`, forwards it (scan_analysis.py:1154) and sets `ax.set_ylim(floor, 2)` (line 1158). All four scan notebooks call `plot_sv_spectra(scan, fig, ax, lr=FOCUS_LR, rtol=rtol)` with no floor. Verified on a synthetic full-width record (B=64, k=16, sigma down to 1e-9): lines drawn = 4 epoch curves clipped to [1e-4, 1], the rtol line and the k line; NO float32 line, ylim (1e-4, 2). So the whole point of the full-spectrum plot -- how far the tail falls below rtol and whether it reaches round-off -- is invisible, and only the unit test (which passes floor=1e-12 explicitly) sees it. The notebooks are not this track's to edit, so the default has to change here.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the floor record-dependent instead of a fixed 1e-4: in `plot_epoch_spectra` default `floor=None` -> `1e-6` for a truncated record and `FLOAT32_NOISE_FLOOR / 10` for a full-width one; stop gating the floor line on `floor` (draw it whenever `full and show_noise_floor`); and in `plot_sv_spectra` set the y limit from the data, e.g. `ax.set_ylim(min(np.nanmin(spectra), style.FLOAT32_NOISE_FLOOR) / 2, 2)`.

findings.issue: `attempted` is `max(manifest count of the FIRST row's config_key, number of rows in the group)`, and `eligible` is now `config_eligible(n_seeds, attempted)` (line 445) instead of `config_eligible(n_seeds, len(self.seeds))`. When the group key is coarser than a run configuration -- `Scan.configs(df, SVEN_CONFIG)` ignores n_train, kappa, microbatch_size, batch_size -- `attempted` becomes the group size and the eligibility threshold changes from 'more than half the SEEDS finished' (CONTRACTS section 1, binding) to 'more than half of all runs in the group'. Reproduced: one k/lr/rtol group spanning two n_train values, 5 seeds each, 4 of 10 finished -> attempted=10, eligible=False, `best_sven()` returns None, where the seed-count rule gives eligible=True. With a manifest the same `max()` also hides missing runs: 2 of 10 runs of a coarse group absent -> attempted=max(5,8)=8, n_missing=0 (truth 2), i.e. the exact invisibility C-A2 was meant to remove. My sweep of all 17 cached + 16 remaining result dirs found no eligibility flip on today's legacy data (so no wrong result yet), but exp_finetune_cifar_smallN, mnist_kappaScan_labelRegression and the microbatch/paramfrac/critbatch dirs all group coarsely (4-16 configs each with attempted > seed count), and the fresh campaign adds manifests. The mirror case also exists: where column grouping is FINER than the run_id (the 5 legacy dirs with F16 schema drift), per_config[key]=5 against a 3-row group reports a phantom n_missing=2.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the expectation from every config_key in the group, not the first row, and never fall back to the group size: `keys = g_all['run_id'].agg(lambda s: {style.config_key(r) for r in s})` then `attempted = sum(per_config[kk] for kk in keys if kk in per_config) or len(self.seeds)`. Same change in analysis_helpers.config_table:194. That restores the CONTRACTS rule exactly when there is no manifest and makes n_missing right when there is one.

findings.issue: `examples_per_epoch` returns `n_train`, but with `drop_last=True` for every optimizer (CONTRACTS, sampler) the examples actually stepped on per epoch are `steps_per_epoch * batch_size`. The fallback branch (line 203) computes exactly that, so the function is self-inconsistent, and the C-A5 'examples processed' axis is wrong whenever n_train % batch_size != 0 -- e.g. small-N points such as n_train=100, B=64 give 64 examples/epoch but are reported as 100 (+56%); MNIST is off by 0.03%. The acceptance test hides it: tests/test_analysis_core.py:588-599 sets steps_per_epoch=25, n_train=800 AND batch_size=8 (mutually inconsistent: 800//8 = 100 steps) and then asserts examples == [800, 1600, 2400, 3200], baking the discrepancy into the expectation.
findings.suggested_fix: `spe = steps_per_epoch(rows); if spe is not None and 'batch_size' in rows.columns and rows['batch_size'].notna().any(): return spe * int(rows['batch_size'].dropna().iloc[0])` and keep `n_train` only as the last resort. Then make the test fixture consistent (steps_per_epoch=100 with n_train=800/B=8, or drop one of the two) so it asserts the product.

findings.issue: C-A2 requires that 'configurations with no result file are no longer invisible', but in the analysis_helpers path they are recorded only on `out.attrs['missing_configs']`, with no print. pandas `.attrs` is dropped by most operations (`tab[tab['eligible']]`, `.head()`, a copy through `.sort_values()`), and the 7 study notebooks (cifar, batchsize, overparam, kappa, critbatch, finetune, nanogpt) that call `config_table` / `best_per_method` never read `.attrs`, so in practice a whole missing configuration stays invisible there. `scan_analysis.load_scan` does print its manifest line (scan_analysis.py:355-360), which is the right pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: After setting the attrs, print one line when non-empty, mirroring load_scan: `mc = out.attrs['missing_configs']; if len(mc): print(f'[config_table] {len(mc)} configuration(s) with no result file at all ({int(mc["n_missing"].sum())} runs): {list(mc["config_key"][:3])}')`.

findings.issue: The test-curve probe uses `_scalar(L, w) is not None`, and `_scalar` returns `np.nan` (not None) when `losses` is not a dict (line 37). A single record whose `losses` is missing/NaN therefore makes the probe true and creates all-NaN `final_test_loss` / `final_test_acc` columns, which then enter OUTCOMES and produce NaN test columns in every config_table. `scan_analysis.__post_init__` (line 306) gets this right with `isinstance(L, dict) and L.get(w) is not None`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same guard: `df['losses'].apply(lambda L, w=which: isinstance(L, dict) and L.get(w) is not None).any()`.

findings.issue: `Scan.configs` and `analysis_helpers.config_table` (line 184) now index `g_all['run_id']` unconditionally, so a table without a `run_id` column raises KeyError where the old code worked. `style.missing_run_ids` guards this case explicitly (`if 'run_id' in df.columns`), so the codebase is inconsistent about it. All 33 real result dirs have run_id (checked), so this is a robustness concern for hand-built frames -- e.g. other tracks' analysis/budget.py and analysis/paired.py pass their own frames into `config_table`.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the `_key` join when `'run_id' not in df.columns` and fall back to `len(self.seeds)` / `df[seed_col].nunique()` for `attempted`.

findings.issue: The opt-in real-scan test loads from `experiment_results` with `cache_dir=os.environ.get('SV3_CACHE_DIR')`, i.e. None unless the caller sets it, which sends the slim-cache write back into `experiment_results/_cache/` -- against the contract rule 'never touch experiment_results/'. It is a no-op today because valid caches exist for both scans, but any file change under those dirs (a rerun landing during the campaign) turns the test into a writer inside the live results root, concurrently with the jobs writing there.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the cache to the test's own tmp dir: `cache_dir=os.environ.get('SV3_CACHE_DIR') or str(tmp_path / 'cache')` (add the `tmp_path` fixture to the test signature), keeping the env var as the fast-path override.

2. The two opt-in real-scan cases, run locally instead of through SLURM by copying `experiment_results/_cache/*.pkl` into my scratchpad and pointing `SV3_CACHE_DIR` there (so nothing is written under `experiment_results/`): `SV3_CHECK_REAL_SCANS=1 SV3_CACHE_DIR=... pytest tests/test_analysis_core.py -q -k real_scan -s` -> `2 passed, 19 deselected in 17.45s`, printing `toy_1d_scan: 734 runs, 148 groups; sizes [1, 4, 5]` and `mnist_scan_ce: 1040 runs, 208 groups; sizes [5]`. Total 21 passed, matching the implementer's run_cpu_tests.sh line.

Independent verification beyond the track's tests (read-only against the results root, cache redirected outside it):

3. Allow-list vs legacy auto-detection on 17 real scan dirs loaded in full (cifar ce + labelReg, critbatch mnist + nanogpt, finetune, nanogpt speedrun (+timing), mnist kappaScan, mnist_scan_ce (+timing), mnist_scan_labelRegression (+timing), polynomial_scan (+timing), fig5 cifar paramfrac, toy_1d_scan (+timing)): the run->configuration PARTITION is identical in every case (58/58, 84/84, 66/66, 80/80, 32/32, 3/3, 208/208, 200/200, 148/148, ...). Dropped columns are only n_params, n_val, gram_freeze_norm_stats, signed_residual, use_gram, variable_k, none varying inside a group. No best-config change survived NaN-aware comparison. `style.average_over_seeds` is fixed, not regressed (it used to make every run its own group: 290 groups for 290 runs -> 58), and it is imported-but-never-called in all 7 study notebooks.
4. The 16 remaining dirs (13 in full, the four 2000+-file dirs sampled every 12th file): partition unchanged, and -- the check that matters for a sampled read -- NO varying scalar column anywhere falls outside HPARAM/PROVENANCE/BACKEND/OUTCOME, so no knob is silently averaged over. The overparam/batchsize knobs are `mlp_width` and `n_data`, both allow-listed. No notebook concatenates scans and records carry no `dataset` field, so nothing can merge two scans.
5. Reproduced findings 1, 2 and 3 on purpose-built synthetic roots; the numbers are quoted in those findings.
6. Cross-checked the manifest/status contract against the writers: `claims.STATUSES == ("ok","diverged","oom","error")`, `DONE_STATUSES == {ok,diverged}` match style.STATUS_OK/STATUS_DIVERGED/FAILED_STATUSES exactly; `claims.write_manifest` writes `{scan}/manifest/{job}.json` with `run_ids` and the `.tmp-` prefix that `style.manifest_run_ids` skips; `grid.py:331` builds the `_mseed{}_lseed{}` suffix that `style.config_key`'s regex strips; `generic_scan._write_result` opens the jsonl with mode 'w', so a retried run cannot leave two records for one run_id; `_CACHE_VERSION` correctly stays at 3 (the slim schema did not change), which is why the existing caches remain valid.

No commits, no SLURM activity, nothing written under experiment_results/. The two import-time assertions (SVEN_CONFIG/BASELINE_CONFIG subset of HPARAM_COLUMNS) are a good guard and hold.

Also noted for the integrator, below finding severity: `resolve_time_key('auto')` now prefers `train_times` over `epoch_times` (scan_analysis.py:551-565), so a legacy-vs-fresh time-axis comparison silently compares wall time against synchronised training time; and `analysis_helpers._manifest_memo` never invalidates while `Scan` re-reads the manifest per load, so during a live campaign the two paths can disagree until the kernel restarts.
